newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes end firm, sour grades drift lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes end firm, sour grades drift lower.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes firmed to the close on Friday, bolstered by futures buying ahead of the long President's Day weekend in the United States.
Position-squaring and a more bullish outlook for unleaded gasoline prospects aided the crude price as well.
Traders said cash domestic grades featured a steady Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James market, but faltering differentials in the West Texas Sour/Midland and Eugene Island sectors.
Sours were depressed by the return of production at Mobil's Green Canyon platforms, increased Iraqi crude sales and an abundance of West Coast supply, traders said.
March West Texas Intermediate/Cushing closed 40 cents lower at $22.35-45 a barrel.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold between 20-29 cts over the WTI/Cushing marker, compared with differentials above a 30 cts premium at Thursday's close.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was done sparingly at a 20 cts discount to the WTI/Cushing, 10-15 cts lower than Thursday.
Other grades heard WTS sell at $2.45, $2.47 and $2.48 under the WTI/Cushing, 15-20 cts weaker than closing levels recorded on Thursday.
Eugene Island barrels moved at $2.40 under the benchmark, and was bid as weak as $2.50 below the WTI/Cushing.
March Postings Plus moved out in-line with the widening of the March/April roll to 38 cts. The postings sold late at $2.15, and at various prices between $2.08-$2.14 earlier.
